JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .

African startups raised a total of $183 million in October 2026 through 34 funding deals worth at least $100,000 each, according to the monthly report published on November 5 by investment tracking platform Africa: The Big Deal.
The amount represents a 24% decline compared with September and stands 29% below the average monthly funding of $259 million recorded over the past 12 months.
The slowdown was even more pronounced year-on-year. Funding fell by 58% from the $435 million raised by African startups in October 2025. The number of announced transactions also declined, with 34 deals recorded in October, against a monthly average of 43 over the past year.
Equity financing accounts for 60% of October funding
Equity investments dominated fundraising activity, accounting for $110 million, or 60% of the total raised during the month.
Debt financing amounted to $71 million, representing 39% of total funding, while grants accounted for approximately $2 million.
The two largest transactions each reached $40 million and were concluded outside Africa’s four leading startup funding markets: Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa.
In Morocco, health tech company ABA Life secured a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African investment fund Admaius Capital Partners.
Founded in 2021, the company develops solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technologies, telemedicine and connected healthcare infrastructure. The funding will support its artificial intelligence programme for healthcare systems and facilitate its international expansion.
In Tanzania, agritech platform East Africa Foods raised nearly $40 million to expand its processing, storage and logistics capabilities, as well as its digital tools.
The company works with more than 28,000 small-scale farmers and supplies over 10,000 urban retailers. It plans to use the financing to expand into additional East African markets.
Nigeria leads African startup funding
Nigeria topped the continental ranking in October, with nine startups raising a combined $42 million, primarily through debt financing in the energy and mobility sectors.
Morocco and Tanzania followed with $40 million each, largely driven by the two major transactions involving ABA Life and East Africa Foods.
Egypt ranked fourth with $19 million, followed by Senegal with $13 million.
A notable shift in funding distribution was also recorded. Startups based in Africa’s four largest funding markets attracted just 46% of total capital raised in October, their lowest monthly share since November 2022.
Nevertheless, these four markets still accounted for 26 of the 34 startups that announced funding rounds of at least `$100,000 during the month.
Climate technology companies were another major beneficiary, attracting 55% of the funding announced in October.
African startups raise $2.4 billion in first 10 months
Between January and October 2026, African startups raised a cumulative $2.4 billion, down 12% from the $2.7 billion recorded during the same period in 2025.
However, the figures reveal contrasting trends between financing instruments. Equity funding increased by 5% year-on-year to $1.6 billion, while debt financing dropped by 33% to $740 million, compared with $1.1 billion a year earlier.
The number of funded startups also declined. A total of 343 companies announced funding rounds of at least $100,000 during the first 10 months of 2026, against 438 in the corresponding period of 2025, representing a 22% decrease.
The number of identified active investors fell by 16%, from 442 to more than 370.
With only two months remaining in the year, African startups would need to raise an additional $814 million in November and December to match the $3.2 billion secured in 2025, a target that Africa: The Big Deal considers unlikely.
Equity financing, however, could exceed its 2025 level. An additional $338 million would be sufficient to surpass the $1.9 billion raised through equity investments last year.

candidates.text:
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. Like MaxCyte, Akron has become a trusted supplier to leading biopharma companies by delivering differentiated, high-quality products and best-in-class service. Akron is a market leader in the mission-critical consumables required for cell therapy manufacturing, including cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived products and media. We are excited to work alongside the talented Akron team as we bring together two companies to deepen customer relationships and better support cell therapy developers from development through commercialization.”
Maher Masoud, President and CEO of MaxCyte
“We are tremendously excited by the opportunity to join these two world-class organizations, leveraging our collective experience and expertise to support our partners as they bring transformative therapies to patients around the world. At Akron, we have always believed in earning our partners’ trust through consistent execution, uncompromising quality, and a deep commitment to the patients they serve. As part of MaxCyte, we remain committed to delivering the quality, reliability, and innovation our partners have come to expect.”
Ezequiel Zylberberg, COO of Akron Bio
“Akron Bio’s success reflects the dedication of its team, and we believe MaxCyte is the best partner to drive continued growth and expand its impact on patients. Our decision to accept MaxCyte shares as part of the consideration reflects our confidence in the combined company’s long-term value and allows us to participate in its future success.”
Arcline Investment Management

candidates.title: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech
candidates.snippet: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech Hoodline
candidates.text:
555 12th St. — Oakland Street Scene
Google Street View
An Oakland health-tech company has raised $140 million in a new funding round. Vumedi, which builds an AI-powered learning platform for physicians, has raised $140 million in Series B funding, with plans to pour the money into talent, research and development, product development and outreach as it expands its clinical learning tools.
The investment came from Oak HC/FT, according to FinSMEs , which reported the round. Vumedi is led by founder and CEO Roman Giverts, and the company describes its platform as a tool that connects clinicians with specialists and peers so they can learn procedures, evaluate treatments and navigate complex cases, the outlet reports.
What the Platform Actually Does
At the center of Vumedi's pitch is scale paired with AI. The platform uses artificial intelligence to turn more than 100,000 physician-led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes, spanning more than 21 medical specialties, into what the company calls an on-demand clinical resource, per the same report. Rather than leaving clinicians to sift through hours of footage, the system synthesizes multiple expert perspectives and links directly to time-stamped segments within videos.
The company says its platform now serves more than 150,000 NPI-verified clinicians and generated over 56 million minutes of learning over the past 12 months. Back in a 2018 interview, Giverts described Vumedi's mission as helping physicians make the best care decisions through what he called unbiased video education in an interview with MPO-mag.com . That same article reported the platform then had roughly 250,000 physician users and 20,000 videos contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare organizations and professionals, including partnerships with 150 hospitals and conferences such as Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins.
Funding Figures Don't All Line Up
Not every account of Vumedi's fundraising history tells the same story. A snippet from 01net referenced a $104 million investment from Oak HC/FT, though it's unclear from that report whether it describes the same financing as the newly reported $140 million round or a separate transaction. Separately, CB Insights lists Vumedi's most recent funding round as a $79.98 million Series B dated May 22, 2025, and puts the company's total raised at $82.08 million across four rounds. The available reporting does not reconcile these differing figures with the $140 million sum reported this week.
Part of a Broader AI Health-Tech Wave
Vumedi's raise lands amid a broader uptick in digital-health investment. Companies in the sector raised $7.4 billion in the first half of 2026, up roughly $1 billion from the same period in 2025, according to Fierce Healthcare . The outlet counted 244 completed deals in that window, with $4.2 billion invested in the first quarter and $3.2 billion in the second.
A notable share of that capital came in the form of megadeals. Nineteen companies raised 20 financings of at least $100 million in the first half of 2026, representing 45 percent of all capital invested, Fierce Healthcare reported, citing deals that included AI radiology company Aidoc's $150 million raise. Clinical-reference platform OpenEvidence, a comparable player in physician-facing AI tools, announced its own $210 million Series B at a $3.5 billion valuation in mid-2025, co-led by Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins with Sequoia Capital, Coatue, Conviction and Thrive also participating, according to a release distributed via PR Newswire . That company said it planned to use its funding to expand strategic content partnerships feeding its medical knowledge library, a goal that echoes Vumedi's own stated plans to grow its content, features and formats.
For now, Vumedi's leadership has framed the new capital as fuel for expansion rather than a pivot. The company's stated plans, per FinSMEs, center on investing in people and product to expand its AI-driven video and podcast library.

candidates.title: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce
candidates.snippet: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce Wowtale
candidates.text:
When AI shopping assistants find, compare and pay for products, brands risk losing their direct relationship with customers. McKinsey projects that agentic commerce could mediate up to $1 trillion in U.S. retail revenue by 2030. Imprint , which builds co-branded credit cards so brands can stay part of everyday spending, has raised $130 million.
Co-branded cards, built from the ground up
Imprint is a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform that helps brands make every transaction more valuable. Founded in 2020 and based in New York, it builds co-branded credit cards with brands and owns its stack across origination, risk, servicing and rewards. That gives brands control of their financial products and room to tailor rewards, the company says.
Since the start of the year it has launched programs with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger and Shell, with the Fanatics card debuting this week. Booking.com is also a customer. Imprint reports more than two million members and partners whose annual U.S. consumer spending exceeds $500 billion. Total cardholder spending across its partners more than doubled between 2025 and 2026, and the share of spending on Imprint cards at partner checkouts tripled in a year. It also added $1.5 billion in warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitization, with demand nearly five times the offering size. These figures come from the company.
For the AI era, Imprint released a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents securely reach members’ rewards, virtual cards and transaction history, along with tools for members to review and authorize agent-initiated purchases. Imprint Access, launching today, gives customers who are new to credit or rebuilding it, backed by a refundable deposit, the same ongoing rewards as a brand’s unsecured card, with a path to upgrade. The Federal Reserve estimates 32 million Americans have little or no credit history.
A law graduate from Dublin who came to cards through WeWork
Founder and CEO Daragh Murphy is Irish, studied law at University College Dublin and was a vice president of operations and strategy at WeWork, according to Irish media. He founded Imprint in 2020 with Gaurav Ahuja and Michael Pechman. Ahuja, a partner at Thrive Capital , is reported to have helped incubate the company and to serve as chairman. Imprint raised a $75 million Series C at a $600 million valuation in October 2024, and press reports put its December 2025 Series D at $150 million and a $1.2 billion valuation.
Valuation up from $1.2B
Imprint said it raised $130 million at a valuation of about $1.9 billion. Existing investor Khosla Ventures led. Existing investors Hedosophia , Ribbit Capital , Spice and Thrive Capital took part, and Positive Sum joined as a new investor. The money will fund new payment options and AI capabilities, so brands can recognize and reward customers however they choose to pay. The release did not name the round.
CEO Murphy said brands that invest in understanding each customer and building individual relationships will win as every digital touchpoint becomes personalized. Patrick O’Shaughnessy, CEO and partner at Positive Sum, said AI makes every option easier to compare, so earning a customer’s preference matters more, and that the team’s full-stack technology and marquee partners gave the firm conviction. Fanatics CFO Glenn Schiffman said Imprint’s technology made it possible to design a card around fans.
Competitors
In U.S. rewards cards, Bilt Rewards is the most visible rival. It started as a card that turns rent into points and raised $250 million in July 2025 at a $10.75 billion valuation, led by General Catalyst and GID. It was reported to be ending its relationship with Wells Fargo and moving its cards to Cardless. No new round since 2026 could be confirmed.
Large issuers that have long run retailer co-brand programs, such as Synchrony and Bread Financial , compete for the same brands. Imprint pitches its own technology stack as the edge in designing products. Among companies we have covered, Ramp approaches cards through corporate spend management and raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation last month.

Clara Raises $105 Million to Grow Latin American Corporate Spend Management Platform
By Julie Muhn (@julieschicktanz) Posted on November 13, 2026
Categories: Daily news , Funding
Clara raised $105 million, comprising a $65 million Series C equity round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility, bringing its total debt and equity funding to $838 million.
Clara will use the funding to expand its market reach and enhance its AI capabilities, including its MCP integration that enables AI agents to access financial data and execute authorized transactions.
The funding comes amid global growth in corporate card and spend management platforms, as providers expand beyond payments and expense tracking to offer integrated, AI-powered financial management tools.
Brazil-based spend management platform Clara raised $105 million this week. The round is comprised of $65 million in equity in a Series C round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF).
The $65 million Series C was anchored by Citius, Kaszek, and DEG, a subsidiary of Germany’s KfW Group. The round also attracted participation from 10 existing investors and three new investors, including CMT Digital and Nascent VC.
The latest investment brings Clara’s total debt and equity funding to $838 million, following several debt financing deals over the past year. In November 2025, Clara secured $70 million in structured debt financing from BBVA Spark, Covalto, and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). Three months later, the company renewed a $150 million credit facility with Goldman Sachs, bringing its total debt capacity to more than $250 million.
Clara will use today’s funding to expand its go-to-market team and strengthen the automation and AI capabilities of its platform. Clara was founded in 2020 and now helps more than 45,000 businesses automate routine work, control spending, and make better financial decisions. The company’s platform offers corporate cards, bill payments, spend management, accounts payable, and accounts receivable to help businesses make and manage payments. Along with the financing announcement, Clara said it has also surpassed $100 million in annualized net revenue and maintained positive EBITDA for more than a year.
Among Clara’s capabilities is its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, which connects the platform with AI agents to enable customers to access real-time spending reports and forecasts using natural language, as well as execute authorized transactions autonomously. The company also offers AI-powered policy enforcement that checks employee expenses against company policies in real time, global spend management tools that allow businesses to manage expenses across countries and currencies, and fleet management solutions that support fuel payments and vehicle operations.
“Clara exists to champion Latin American businesses, and we work tirelessly to give them the tools to compete and win on the global stage,” said Clara Co-Founder and CEO Gerry Giacomán Colyer. “The region has long been underserved by financial platforms designed for other markets. We’re combining AI with local expertise to solve challenges specific to doing business here and give our customers a distinct competitive edge.”
Clara’s latest funding comes as spend management platforms increasingly look beyond corporate cards and expense tracking. By combining payments, financial data, and AI-driven automation, Clara is positioning itself to help businesses manage not just how they spend money, but how they make financial decisions.
The news of Clara’s growth comes as corporate card and spend management fintechs around the world are expanding their customer bases as well as their offerings. Companies such as Ramp and Brex in the US, Pleo and Payhawk in Europe, and Airwallex in Asia-Pacific have expanded beyond corporate cards to offer more comprehensive financial management platforms. These providers have integrated payments, expense management, accounts payable, and AI-powered automation into a single offering. Clara is following a similar trajectory in Latin America, where its regional focus and growing suite of financial tools position it to compete for businesses looking to consolidate and automate their financial operations.

SALT LAKE CITY , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Databento, the market data platform for modern finance, today announced a $100 million Series C financing at a $1.1 billion valuation. The round was led by Fifth Down Capital, an early investor in Databento, with participation from nearly all of the company's existing investors, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital, and Hedosophia.
The announcement follows Databento's $97 million Series B earlier this year. Since closing its previous round, the company has more than doubled its revenue while remaining profitable.
Databento serves leading quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities firms, and digital asset companies. The company has also established a strong presence in artificial intelligence, having signed enterprise contracts with five of the six leading frontier AI labs.
Databento had 39 employees when it closed its Series C, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation with a fraction of the headcount of traditional market data providers.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry," said Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO of Databento. "Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow."
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data," said Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital. "Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing."
The round also included a strategic investment from Fitch Ventures, bringing the perspective of a leading financial information provider with deep expertise in credit ratings, financial data, and market insights.
"Financial data is becoming increasingly API-driven and machine-consumed, creating an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how institutions and other market participants access it," said Gabby Munoz, Global Head of M&A and Venture Investments at Fitch Group. "Databento has built differentiated infrastructure at the source and paired it with a modern, self-service model that makes institutional-grade market data available on demand. We're excited to back the team as they scale a platform we believe will help shape how market data is captured, delivered, and consumed."
The new funding will support Databento's continued investment in its market data infrastructure and expansion into additional asset classes.
About Databento
Databento is the market data platform for modern finance. The company provides real-time and historical data across futures, options, equities, and indices through a unified API. By owning the entire stack from source to delivery, Databento is the first platform of its kind to combine the performance and reliability demanded by the world's leading trading firms with a dramatically simpler developer experience. Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation,
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, with participation from Prosperity7 Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco.
The round was co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory participating alongside new investors, including Databricks Ventures.
From Customer Data to AI-Powered Sales Execution
Rox develops AI revenue agents designed to help large enterprises identify commercial opportunities, generate sales pipelines and automate customer-facing workflows.
Its platform supports tasks ranging from prospect research and lead qualification to personalized outreach, meeting scheduling, deal management and account expansion.
The agents operate within companies’ existing systems and leverage enterprise customer data to support sales execution.
Rather than simply generating recommendations or content, Rox aims to enable AI agents to take action across revenue workflows and deliver measurable commercial outcomes.
ARR Grew More Than 10x in Its First Year
Rox said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew more than tenfold in its first year in the market, as the platform expanded across enterprise customers in technology, energy, industrial and financial services sectors.
Its customer base includes companies such as Groq, Ramp and Puma Energy. Rox also reported net revenue retention exceeding 700% among enterprise customers, reflecting significant expansion in revenue from existing accounts.
The company is positioning its platform around measurable business impact, including pipeline generation, customer engagement and sales productivity.
Funding to Accelerate AI Research and Enterprise Expansion
Rox plans to use the new capital to advance AI research, develop custom models and strengthen its evaluation infrastructure for real-world revenue tasks.
The company also intends to expand its enterprise customer base across healthcare, industrial manufacturing, financial services, energy and technology.
Why AI Revenue Agents Are Attracting Investors
The funding highlights a broader shift in enterprise AI, from tools that generate content or assist employees to agents capable of executing complex workflows and connecting data with business actions.
Sales is emerging as a major application area because it involves extensive customer data, repetitive administrative tasks and multiple interconnected processes, from prospecting to account management.
However, the long-term opportunity for Rox will depend on its ability to demonstrate sustainable customer returns, scale enterprise deployments and compete with established customer relationship management platforms.
The investment underscores growing venture capital interest in AI agents that can deliver measurable operational and commercial outcomes, positioning autonomous enterprise workflows as a major frontier in AI adoption.

candidates.snippet: Adaspace Hong Kong IPO Raises $95.6 Million for AI Satellites iNews Zoombangla
candidates.text:
Adaspace Technology raised HK$750 million ($95.6 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, and its shares moved higher by the midday break after opening below the offer price. The debut puts a listed supplier of AI-powered satellites and satellite-data services on the market as the company seeks funding for research, production and facilities.
Reuters reported that the shares opened at HK$24.44, 1.8% below the HK$24.90 offer price, and were last at HK$24.60 in its morning report. Bamboo Works later reported a rise to HK$25.26 by the midday break, 1.45% above the offer price. Those are snapshots from different points in Friday’s session; neither is a closing price.
The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million shares at HK$24.90 each, the bottom of its marketed range of HK$24.90 to HK$33.20, Reuters reported. The wire also said the retail tranche was subscribed 3.43 times and the international offering was covered 1.79 times. Those figures describe separate parts of the offering and should not be combined as one subscription measure.
Reuters describes Adaspace as a maker of AI-powered satellites that also provides satellite-data services. The Hong Kong exchange’s November 12 global-offering announcement identifies Adaspace Technology and refers investors to the company’s November 5 prospectus. The filing is the primary record for the offering; Reuters and Bamboo Works provide independent reports on the first trading session.
Bamboo Works reported net proceeds of HK$652 million ($83.6 million). It said the company plans to use 35.6% of that amount to strengthen research and development, 24.4% to build a center in Shenzhen, 20% for strategic investments and acquisitions, and 10% to repay bank loans. These are the allocations listed in the report; they do not account for every part of the proceeds.
The same report gave a snapshot of the company’s recent finances. Adaspace recorded first-half 2026 revenue of 226 million yuan ($33.9 million), down 6.3% from a year earlier. Its net loss narrowed 21.5% to 150 million yuan. The revenue decline and narrower loss are separate measures, so the loss reduction does not mean revenue grew.
For the Adaspace Hong Kong IPO, the distinction between the amount raised and the net proceeds matters: Reuters reported the HK$750 million raise, while Bamboo Works cited HK$652 million in net proceeds. The reports also show a share price that first fell below the offer price and later moved above it by midday, without establishing the final close.
The debut marks the start of public trading for the company’s shares, while the planned research, production and Shenzhen spending remain future uses of the funds. The available reports do not establish how quickly those investments will translate into additional satellites, data services or revenue. They document the offering terms, early trading and the company’s stated financial results, leaving later operating performance to subsequent disclosures.

Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 12, 2026
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
Eli Radiopharma has raised nearly $60 million (RMB 400 million) in Series A financing to advance its radiopharmaceutical pipeline toward clinical development. The funding will support preclinical research, regulatory submissions, early-stage clinical studies, and the expansion of the company’s research and development capabilities.
Huagai Capital led the financing round, with Bayland Capital serving as co-lead investor. Additional participants included Boyu Ventures, Delian Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Haibang Venture, Bairui Capital, Shenzhen Angel FOF Management, and Grand Flight Investment.
Existing shareholders CSPC & Growth Bio Fund, Huaige Capital, KHK Fund, Longfeng Venture, Hongsheng Capital, Bioclub Fund, and Skyfield Capital also participated in the financing.
Eli Radiopharma plans to allocate the proceeds toward preclinical research, investigational new drug applications, and early-stage clinical development. The company will also strengthen its research platforms, recruit additional talent, expand clinical operations, and pursue business development opportunities.
Founded in 2024, Eli Radiopharma focuses on developing radiopharmaceutical products that combine molecular targeting with radionuclide technology. Its pipeline includes diagnostic and therapeutic candidates designed to address unmet medical needs in oncology and neurological diseases.
The company has advanced multiple programs targeting novel molecular mechanisms through lead discovery, laboratory validation, and animal studies. Several candidates are approaching investigational new drug submissions, representing an important transition from early research toward human clinical testing.
Radiopharmaceuticals combine targeting molecules with radioactive isotopes to identify or treat diseased tissue. Therapeutic radioligands are designed to deliver radiation directly to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Related diagnostic imaging agents can help physicians identify appropriate patients, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment responses.
The financing also reflects growing international interest in radiopharmaceutical innovation originating in China. Global pharmaceutical companies have increasingly explored opportunities involving novel molecular targets, therapeutic radionuclides, and expanded clinical applications.
Eli Radiopharma’s investors identified these areas as important drivers of future industry growth, particularly as radiopharmaceutical technologies move into additional cancer indications and other therapeutic applications.
The company’s longer-term strategy includes building a globally competitive pipeline capable of serving patients in international markets, including the U.S. and Europe. Its immediate priorities involve completing preclinical development, meeting regulatory requirements, and advancing differentiated candidates into clinical studies.
The Series A financing provides Eli Radiopharma with additional resources to move its lead programs closer to clinical validation while expanding the infrastructure needed to support a broader radiopharmaceutical development portfolio.

LOS ANGELES , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kindo , the run-anywhere AI agent management platform that puts the enterprise in control, today announced a $30 million raise co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing total capital raised to $57.6 million. The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.

Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. For mission-critical agents that need deeper control, Kindo's harness, purpose-built for centralized agent operations, adds around-the-clock monitoring, support, and direct intervention, including the ability to take over an agent when something goes wrong.
Customer Adoption
Kindo runs in production at large and mid-market enterprises in financial services, professional services, healthcare, and aviation/transportation. Global aviation in-flight data provider Aireon's CISO reported in May 2026 that using Kindo for threat hunting and Tier 1 and Tier 2 SOC functions helped the company work faster, get more value from its existing security monitoring infrastructure, and save more than $2 million a year.
Controlling AI Cost
Security and compliance were the first reasons organizations needed control of their agents. Cost is now front and center. AI spend is growing year over year with no end in sight, and it has become a key issue slowing AI programs.
Kindo's AI Control Center gives Finance teams a way in. Every token consumed and every agent run's outcome is recorded, including the failed ones, so costs and return on AI spend roll up by individual, agent, department, and project. Budgets can be set, alerts triggered, and hard spend caps enforced. Finance sees what each agent is trying to do, what it did, and how much it spent doing it, which surfaces the agents that fail often, deliver little, or use models that are overkill for the task.
For agents running in Kindo's harness, the Deep Hat add-ons drive those costs down. Deep Hat Sift learns from an agent's verdicts which events on busy alert and ticket queues it would dismiss; once a person approves the threshold, Sift skips those runs, logs every event it filters, and sends a sample through to measure misses. Deep Hat Tune adapts a smaller, lower-cost model to a specific task, reserving larger models for work that needs them. Deep Hat Shrink runs repeatable workflow steps as code, eliminating the model cost entirely, and still routes exceptions back to the model when needed. Deep Hat Attack gives security teams low-cost, private offensive security testing, reducing frontier cybersecurity model use for day-to-day security work.

British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
By Amit Chowdhry

British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The investment supports the first closing of Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II. Commitments to the fund and its related co-investment vehicles now total approximately £120 million.
Harwood will use the capital to provide debt financing for privately held companies pursuing organic expansion, acquisitions, and shareholder transitions. The strategy gives business owners an alternative to conventional bank lending or a complete sale through an M&A transaction.
The commitment increases the British Business Bank’s total investment with Harwood to £75 million. The government-owned development bank previously committed £35 million to the manager’s inaugural HPC UK SME Fund in 2020.
Harwood specializes in flexible private-credit solutions for lower-middle-market companies. Its target borrowers include founder- and family-owned businesses that need additional growth capital but want to preserve ownership and strategic control.
The inaugural fund invested across digital technology, clean-energy supply chains, manufacturing, tourism, and other sectors. One portfolio example is Western Marinas, a Welsh marina operator that used Harwood financing to restore facilities in Wales and southwest England.
That investment supported local jobs and family-operated businesses while attracting visitors and economic activity to surrounding coastal communities. It demonstrates how private credit can finance physical assets and regional companies that may not fit the standardized requirements of traditional lenders.
The British Business Bank’s mandate is to improve access to capital for smaller companies and address financing gaps that can limit growth, productivity, and job creation. In its 2025-2026 financial year, the bank supported £9.4 billion of financing for approximately 38,000 businesses.
That total included £1.3 billion of public funding, £4.3 billion of private capital attracted through the bank’s programs, and £3.7 billion of guaranteed lending. Around 30,000 recipients had not previously received support through the institution.

The company believes training AI systems on information closely connected to actual patient biology can support more relevant drug development research.

Ex-Tesla Engineer’s SE3 Raises $30M for Drone AI Built for Any Drone
Posted on November 13, 2026 November 12, 2026 by Flavia Moura
13
Nov
The Munich startup is the only serious bidder for the battlefield command screen that sells nothing underneath it. Ukraine approved a new drone model about every 10 hours this year. That is the whole pitch, and the whole problem.
SE3, a Munich spinout from the Technical University of Munich, raised a $30 million Series A led by Accel to build AI that runs drones from any manufacturer. The bet is that militaries will pay for neutrality as their fleets splinter. Ukraine codified 650 new drone systems in the first 265 days of 2026.
Picture a Bundeswehr operator in 2028. Her unit flies quadcopters from one German startup, fixed-wing scouts from another, loitering munitions from a third, and a couple of ground robots nobody remembers ordering. Each one shipped with its own app. Now she wants to say, out loud, “send something to look two kilometers north over that forest,” and have the right machine take off.
That sentence is the product SE3 is selling. The hard part is not the voice command. It is that the machine she wants could have been built by anyone.
What Happened
Fortune reported on November 12 that SE3, which recently dropped “Labs” from its name, closed a $30 million Series A led by Accel, with Keen, Lakestar and Seedcamp joining. Valuation, revenue and total funding were not disclosed.
The round lands fast. SE3 came out of stealth on June 26, 2026, with a €5.5 million seed (about $6.1 million) led by Lakestar, alongside Seedcamp, EWOR, the Sequoia Scout Fund and Plug and Play. That is roughly 4.9 times the seed check, raised 139 days later.
The basics:
Who: CEO Lukas Köstler, a former TUM PhD student who worked on Tesla’s Autopilot team and at Nvidia Research; CTO Simon Klenk, his TUM labmate; and chief science officer Daniel Cremers, who runs the computer vision lab the company spun out of.
What it builds: software that fuses video and sensor feeds from many drones and ground vehicles into one 3D map, labels what is in it, and lets soldiers query it or task machines by voice. It also builds onboard autonomy for navigation when GPS is jammed, object detection and swarm behavior.
Who pays: the Bundeswehr, under contracts to develop fleet command AI, plus Ukraine, where the technology is already deployed. Partners include sensor maker Hensoldt, drone software company Auterion and drone developer ERC.
What the money buys: headcount goes from about 40 to about 120, with new offices in London, Berlin, the Nordics and Baltics, and Poland.
Köstler described the shared map to Fortune as working “like a mini map, how you would know it from a strategy game.” Gamers will get it instantly. Procurement officers will get it the moment they price what happens when that mini map only shows one vendor’s units.
The Backstory
Every outlet will frame this as another European defense AI round riding rearmament money. True, and not very useful. The more interesting fact is the market structure SE3 is walking into.
Start with Ukraine, the world’s largest live test of drone procurement. Its Ministry of Defence codified 413 unmanned aerial systems in the first half of 2026, up more than 30% on the same period of 2025 and more than 73% on 2024. By September 22 the count was 650. Strike copters alone accounted for 238 new models, interceptors 42, deep-strike drones nine.
Run the division nobody ran: 650 systems over the 265 days from January 1 to September 22 is about 2.45 a day, or one new approved model roughly every 9.8 hours.
Every one of those airframes is one more thing a command screen has to talk to. Someone writes that integration, then rewrites it when the firmware changes, then does it again for the next model. That is a lot of glue code for a single army.
Germany, SE3’s anchor customer, is building the same diversity on purpose. On February 25, the Bundestag’s budget committee approved framework deals worth about €270 million each for Helsing’s HX-2 and Stark Defence’s Virtus loitering munitions, two different airframes from two different startups for the same mission. Option ceilings reached €1.46 billion for Helsing and €2.86 billion for Stark, per procurement documents reported by the Financial Times. Berlin also financed a deal of roughly €90 million for Auterion to equip 50,000 Ukrainian strike drones built by manufacturer Skyfall.
Dual-sourcing is sensible procurement. It also manufactures the exact problem a neutral software layer solves.
The Plan: Own the Map, Rent the Model
The architecture is where SE3 makes its most deliberate business choice.
It does not ask a general-purpose large language model to understand terrain or physics. Classical computer vision turns raw sensor data into a structured database of objects and their relationships. A language model then queries that database and calls conventional tools, such as a planning algorithm that computes a flight path around mountains and out of enemy lines of sight. Köstler told Fortune that feeding raw sensor data straight into a model would not work at all.
Three consequences follow, and they are all about cost and control rather than cleverness:
The expensive asset is the map, not the model. Perception and the structured database are what SE3 builds and owns. The language model is an interface sitting on top.
The model is swappable. Customers can plug in their preferred frontier model, and the whole system can run fully offline. SE3 treats the AI lab as a replaceable supplier.
Humans stay in the approval loop. Actions such as a drone takeoff can require operator sign-off, which matters for European buyers answering to parliaments.

SHENZHEN, China , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clawlab, a technology startup developing smart tools for textile creation, has raised more than $15 million in a Pre-A3 funding round led by miHoYo. Vision Plus Capital and Shunwei Capital also increased their investments through super pro rata participation. The round brings Clawlab's total funding to approximately $25 million across four equity rounds. Its shareholder base includes Sequoia China, Shunwei Capital, YM Capital, Vision Plus Capital, and miHoYo, bringing together leading venture capital firms and a strategic corporate investor.
Investors Back Clawlab's Vision for a New Consumer Category
With AI software commanding much of the market's attention, Clawlab's more than $15 million funding round reflects investor interest in a different opportunity: the untapped consumer potential of smart knitting.
The opportunity comes from a gap between rising consumer demand and the tools available to meet it. Interest in personalized, hands-on creation is growing, yet most knitting equipment remains designed for factories and professional users. Pattern development, stitch control, and machine operation still require specialist expertise. The category lacks a desktop device capable of bringing industrial-grade knitting capabilities within reach of individual creators.
Clawlab is addressing that gap with the world's first smart knitting machine designed for home use. It turns an image or idea into a finished knitted item, handling pattern preparation, stitchwork, and repetitive production while leaving the design, colors, and intended use to the user.
That flexibility supports a wide range of applications, from scarves and doll clothes to pet accessories and personalized gifts. A hobby project can also grow into custom work or a small business. Clawlab is set to unveil this smart knitting machine to a global audience at CES 2027.
The Engineering Foundation Behind Clawlab
Bringing professional knitting equipment into the home involves more than reducing its size. The real challenge is translating complex engineering into a product that feels intuitive to everyday users. Clawlab's founder and CEO Wenxin Hu previously worked as a hardware engineer at DJI and Meituan, while most members of the company's core R&D team are also former DJI employees. Together, they bring experience developing consumer-grade smart hardware and other technically complex products.
That background has shaped Clawlab's approach to product development. Rather than simply miniaturizing existing equipment or adding digital features, the company is rethinking the knitting experience across hardware, software, and interaction design around the needs of individual creators. The technology takes on the complexity, while users retain control of the creative process.
The Long-Term Vision in Knitting
Clawlab chose knitting based on a simple premise: textiles meet one of the most basic and enduring needs of everyday life.
"Textiles meet a broad, long-standing need in everyday life. Standardized products are abundant, but consumers' desire for personal style, customization, and emotional expression remains underserved," said Wenxin Hu. "We want to reconnect ideas, design, and production so that people without professional training can create through knitting."
Their longer-term ambition is to make knitting an everyday medium of expression. Smart knitting equipment, design software, and a creator community can help people turn ideas, memories, and care for others into one-of-a-kind pieces they can hold, share, and pass on.
About Clawlab
Clawlab is a technology startup founded in 2023 that develops smart tools for textile creation. It is building the future of knitting through a combination of innovative knitting technologies and a connected maker community. Its mission, "Push knitting forward. Bring more ideas to life," is to develop the tools and technology that help more people turn what they imagine into something they can hold. Clawlab's vision is to make knitting an everyday language for expression, much like words and pictures, through which people can tell their stories, preserve memories, and connect with others. For more information, please visit www.clawlab.com

The round was co-led by Radical Ventures and Costanoa, with participation from Tenacity Capital joining high-profile angels Fei-Fei Li, Nobel laureate Guido Imbens, and early employees of Anthropic and OpenAI. . Delphina will use the funding to scale the Context Factory and grow its go-to-market and customer engineering teams.
Delphina was built to meet data teams' standards, but business teams now ask 73% of the questions on the platform, and CEOs at more than half of its customers are active users. At Substack, more than 70% of employees use Delphina, including CEO Chris Best. Other customers include LATAM Airlines, Gen Digital, Upstart, Udemy, Medely, Coursera, and BaseCamp Franchising.
"We want to give our people superpowers with AI. Delphina does that for data," said Chris Best, CEO of Substack. "Now our teams get accurate answers in seconds instead of waiting weeks in a queue. It's changed how we make decisions."
AI analytics is only as good as what it knows about the business: which tables are trusted, how metrics are defined, and what experienced analysts know but never wrote down. Most companies build that context by hand, and it goes stale as the business changes. The Context Factory hands that work to agents. They build a working baseline from a company's existing data and documents in hours, find and fix gaps as people ask questions, and route important changes to domain experts for approval.
"At Uber, everyone, including the CEO, was hands-on with data. That direct line to the numbers was a real advantage, but it took an army of data engineers to keep it from collapsing into chaos," said Jeremy Hermann, Delphina's CEO and co-founder. "The Context Factory gives every company that same advantage. Agents do the heavy lifting, and data teams become the knowledge captains who decide how the business sees its numbers."
"Most companies are data-obsessed but struggle to become data-driven," said Duncan Gilchrist, Delphina's President and co-founder. "When everyone can get trusted answers, everyone suddenly has questions. Ops, sales, marketing and finance teams are now the heaviest users of Delphina, and they keep coming back."
Hermann built and led Uber's Michelangelo machine learning platform and co-founded Tecton, which was acquired by Databricks. Gilchrist led global pricing data science at Uber. The Context Factory is available today at delphina.ai .

Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Mn to Scale AI Agents for Restaurant Businesses
Om Singh
| November 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million in funding from Houston-based Narahari Investments as it looks to expand its artificial intelligence solutions for restaurant businesses.
The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI Catering Sales Agent, the launch of three additional AI agents currently in beta testing, and the development of a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Founded in December 2025 by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy , Kutlerri.ai is developing AI-powered tools to help restaurants generate more sales, control operating expenses and improve profitability. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Unlike conventional software providers that charge fixed subscription fees, Kutlerri.ai follows a performance-linked pricing model. Restaurants are charged based on the additional revenue generated or costs saved through its products.
AI Agent Helps Restaurants Find Catering Customers
Kutlerri.ai’s first commercially available product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, focuses on helping restaurants grow their catering businesses.
The agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant and reaches out to them through emails, text messages and phone calls. It also helps restaurants convert incoming enquiries into catering orders.
The product was developed in collaboration with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group operating in the Washington DC region.
According to Kutlerri.ai, its AI agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over a 10-month period. The startup said the revenue was more than 10 times the amount RASA paid for the service, without requiring the restaurant group to hire additional sales personnel.
Plans to Expand Product Portfolio and Team
Kutlerri.ai currently has one commercially available product, three AI agents undergoing beta testing and two more in development.
The latest funding will help the company accelerate product development, expand its teams and bring additional AI-powered solutions to restaurant operators.
The startup has more than 10 signed customers in the US, which remains its primary market. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also maintains an office in Houston.
Alongside its US expansion, Kutlerri.ai is exploring business opportunities in India and other markets.

Backswing Ventures invests selectively in companies addressing critical challenges across defense and national security. As aerial threats continue to evolve in speed, sophistication, and scale, the ability to detect, track, and intercept them autonomously is becoming increasingly important. Vigilant Works is developing an integrated approach to counter-UAS operations, combining high-speed interception, autonomous guidance, and radar technology into a scalable defense ecosystem.
Founded by a team of engineers and defense technology entrepreneurs, Vigilant Works is developing an autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem combining interceptor platforms, proprietary autonomy technologies, and radar-based detection capabilities. Its first-generation Algiz-1 has undergone battlefield testing, providing operational experience that informs the development of its next-generation systems. The company is currently advancing Algiz-2, a next-generation interceptor capable of speeds exceeding 600 km/h and designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Vigilant Works has recently entered active battlefield testing of Algiz-2 and secured its first commercial agreements outside Ukraine. The company is also developing its proprietary autonomy stack and radar solutions in Ukraine, with investment capital supporting continued technology development and preparations to scale production and operations across NATO-allied countries. The company is a member of Brave1, Ukraine's defense technology coordination platform, and was previously selected for the Brave1 / Ministry of Defence EU4UA program.
"We are excited to support Vigilant Works as they continue developing and scaling their autonomous defense capabilities," said Kyle Asman , Managing Partner at Backswing Ventures. "The evolution of aerial threats is creating an increasingly urgent need for effective counter-UAS solutions. Vigilant Works has the benefit of developing its technology in an environment where these capabilities are being tested against real operational requirements. We believe the team's focus on autonomous interception, radar, and high-speed threats addresses an important and growing need across the defense ecosystem."
"We believe the next leap in counter-UAS will come from rethinking the entire interception chain, much like rocketry did decades ago. Detection, radar, autonomy, and high-speed interception cannot be developed in isolation. We're building them as one integrated system, designed from the ground up to push the boundaries of autonomous air defense," said Daniel Korogodski, CEO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
"Building both the autonomy software and the interceptor platform gives us a unique advantage. We learn directly from Ukraine's best interceptor pilots, turn real-world operational experience into data, and iterate at a pace few can match. We're not just automating today's best pilots, we're building autonomy to outperform them," said Bohdan Boryslavski, CTO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
Vigilant Works is continuing to expand its international footprint while preparing to scale production and operations across allied markets. Erie Strategic Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has announced investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer, two technology companies focused on enterprise AI infrastructure, software modernization, and artificial intelligence security. The investments expand Erie Strategic Ventures’ portfolio of companies developing technologies that can help organizations deploy, manage, and secure AI applications.
Blitzy provides an autonomous software development platform designed to modernize large enterprise codebases through coordinated AI agents. HiddenLayer develops security technology that protects generative, predictive, and agentic AI systems throughout their lifecycles.
The investments reflect Erie Insurance’s continued exploration of AI technologies that could support its operations, independent insurance agents, and policyholders.
Erie Strategic Ventures was launched in August 2022 to invest in companies operating across the personal and commercial insurance value chain, as well as adjacent technology markets.
The venture capital program is operated with support from Cerity Partners Ventures, which helps corporations manage strategic investment initiatives.
Through the program, Erie Insurance combines capital investment with opportunities for technology collaboration and business development.
Blitzy Focuses On Autonomous Software Development
Blitzy develops an AI-powered software engineering platform intended to help enterprises modernize legacy systems and accelerate new application development.
The company’s technology uses a proprietary ontology and graph-based architecture to develop a detailed understanding of large software codebases.
This approach is designed to provide AI systems with contextual information about how applications, components, and dependencies interact.
Using that information, Blitzy coordinates thousands of AI agents operating in parallel to perform software development tasks.
The platform is intended to address challenges associated with maintaining and updating complex enterprise software environments.
Large organizations frequently operate systems that have accumulated years of modifications, integrations, and dependencies.
Modernizing these environments can require significant engineering resources because changes to one component may affect other applications or business processes.
Blitzy’s approach seeks to improve efficiency by enabling AI agents to analyze software architecture and coordinate development activities.
The company also supports the creation of new software products, allowing engineering teams to use autonomous agents for development workflows.
For insurance companies and other financial services organizations, software modernization can be particularly important because many essential business processes depend on established technology systems.
Erie Strategic Ventures’ investment provides exposure to technology intended to improve enterprise software development and infrastructure management.

HiddenLayer focuses on protecting AI systems against cyber threats throughout the development and deployment lifecycle.
Its platform supports security capabilities involving AI discovery, supply chain protection, attack simulation, and runtime defense.
These technologies are designed to help organizations identify and manage vulnerabilities associated with AI applications and infrastructure.
HiddenLayer’s platform addresses generative AI, predictive AI, and autonomous AI agents.
As enterprises integrate AI into business operations, they face security challenges that differ from those associated with conventional software systems.
AI applications can introduce risks involving model manipulation, unauthorized access, sensitive information exposure, and malicious interactions.
HiddenLayer develops tools intended to help security teams identify these risks and establish protective controls.
Its technology is supported by patented capabilities and adversarial AI research.
The platform includes tools for discovering AI systems within an organization and evaluating security weaknesses.
Attack simulation capabilities allow security teams to assess how AI applications may respond to malicious activity.
Runtime protection is designed to help defend deployed AI systems against threats during operation.
HiddenLayer also supports organizations seeking to protect intellectual property and meet applicable regulatory requirements.
The investment aligns with Erie Insurance’s interest in evaluating technologies that can support secure enterprise AI adoption.

Blitzy addresses the development and modernization of the software infrastructure that supports business operations.
